extracted.intended_audience: suspended patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) and counsel handling reinstatement petitions before the USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Administrative decision regarding a petition to reinstate a previously suspended practitioner to practice before the USPTO; focuses on submission of an affidavit certifying compliance with regulatory requirements and the Director's discretionary review. Applicable to practitioners seeking reinstatement under USPTO disciplinary rules (37 C.F.R. § 11.58).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit certifying compliance with the requirements of 37 CFR § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: On September 14, 2012, Mr. Chael filed an Affidavit certifying compliance with the requirements of 37 CFR § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An affidavit certifying compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 is a factual showing required for consideration of reinstatement. This document is submitted with the petition and is a primary basis for the Office's review (the page does not reproduce the text of § 11.58; practitioners should consult the regulation for specific substantive requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing of a Petition for Reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration has been given to the Petition for Reinstatement of Mr. Chael, received on November 13, 2012.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The formal filing of a petition for reinstatement initiates review by the Director of Enrollment and Discipline; the petition should be accompanied by the required affidavit(s) and any supporting materials demonstrating compliance and fitness to resume practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's discretionary review and determination of appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: After careful review of the Petition and Affidavit, the Director of Enrollment and Discipline has determined that reinstatement of Mr. Chael to practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is subject to the Director's discretionary determination based on review of the petition, affidavit(s), and any other relevant materials. If the Director finds reinstatement appropriate, a grant order is issued. The document evidences that compliance plus the petition may lead to reinstatement, but does not detail the standards the Director applies beyond statutory/regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of a prior Final Order of suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: In a Final Order dated August 1, 2012, Mark L. Chael was suspended from practicing patent, trademark and other non-patent law before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prior suspension (Final Order) is the antecedent condition that makes reinstatement proceedings necessary; documentation of the prior suspension and its terms is relevant background for evaluating a reinstatement petition.
